{"concepts_used":["GC-0109","GC-0081","GC-0088","GC-0084","GC-0104"],"decline_reason":"","declined":false,"citations":[{"ref":"TMA1995/s185","quote":"(2) A trade mark may be registered as a defensive trade mark in respect of particular goods or services even if the registered owner does not use or intend to use the trade mark in relation to those goods or services."},{"ref":"TMA1995/s185","quote":"(1) If, because of the extent to which a registered trade mark has been used in relation to all or any of the goods or services in respect of which it is registered, it is likely that its use in relation to other goods or services will be taken to indicate that there is a connection between those other goods or services and the registered owner of the trade mark, the trade mark may, on the application of the registered owner, be registered as a defensive trade mark in respect of any or all of those other goods or services."},{"ref":"TMM/Part34/8#1","quote":"A defensive trade mark may not be removed from the Register on grounds of non-use."},{"ref":"TMM/Part34/10#1","quote":"Although Part 9 (Removal of Trade Mark from Register for Non-use) is not directly applicable to defensive trade marks, it may indirectly be used to attack the defensive registration. An action to cancel or remove the primary trade mark registration upon which the defensive registration is based may be brought, thus enabling the provisions of sections 88 and 189 of the Act to be invoked for the purpose of cancelling the defensive registration."},{"ref":"TMM/Part34/10#1","quote":"Section 189 states that the Registrar may cancel registration of a trade mark as a defensive trade mark if the trade mark is not otherwise registered in the name of the registered owner of the defensive trade mark."}],"answer":"No intention to use is required for the goods or services covered by the defensive registration, and the defensive registration cannot be directly removed for non-use. There is, however, a possible indirect vulnerability through the underlying registration.

• Act — intention to use: Section 185(2) expressly permits defensive registration even where the registered owner does not use or intend to use the mark for those particular goods or services. [TMA1995/s185]

• Act — underlying use still matters: This does not dispense with the qualifying use required by section 185(1). The existing registered mark must have been used to such an extent that use for the other goods or services would likely indicate a connection with its registered owner. [TMA1995/s185]

• Manual practice — direct non-use removal: The Manual states that a defensive trade mark may not be removed from the Register on grounds of non-use. [TMM/Part34/8#1]

• Manual practice — indirect cancellation risk: The Manual explains that cancellation or removal of the primary registration may enable cancellation of the defensive registration under sections 88 and 189. Its account of section 189 says the Registrar may cancel where the mark is not otherwise registered in the defensive registration owner's name. This is the Manual's explanation; the text of sections 88 and 189 has not been supplied here. [TMM/Part34/10#1]"}
